Hi Neha,

We're preparing Acme Health's vendor packet for our pilot and need to confirm a few privacy items before legal can sign off:

- Can Redwood execute a US state privacy addendum (service provider / processor language) that mirrors the CPRA/CCPA requirements (no sale, limited retention, data subject request support)? I've attached Acme's template with the typical redlines.
- Please provide a current subprocessors list and indicate your notification cadence for additions.
- We also need to confirm your stance on data transfers — if any patient metadata leaves the US, what safeguards apply? Do you rely on SCCs / standard contractual clauses for EU/UK data?

Attached: Acme_DPA_Redline_2025-08-01.docx (redlined vendor DPA and a short addendum).

Timing: procurement would like a confirmed DPA to attach to the PO by the week of Aug 11. Can you confirm who's best to coordinate (legal or sales)?

Thanks —
Liam

Hi Liam / Sarah —

Attached is Redwood's current DPA (Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf) and our subprocessors export (subprocessors_list_2025-07.csv). A few quick notes:

- We accept "service provider / processor" terminology and will not change the fundamental sale definition — Redwood does not sell personal information as defined under CCPA/CPRA.
- Subprocessors: we maintain a public list and provide a CSV snapshot on request. Typical additions: cloud infra, observability, and third-party model hosting partners. We provide 30 days' notice for any new subprocessors that materially process customer content.
- Transfers: for EU/UK transfers we rely on SCCs when necessary; for US-based transfers within our platform no international transfer mechanism is needed.

DocuSign: I'm also sending the DPA via DocuSign here: https://www.docusign.net/link/to/redwood-dpa — sign and return when ready.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf, subprocessors_list_2025-07.csv

Thanks Priyom — we reviewed Redwood_DPA_v3 and have a couple of relatively minor asks captured in the attached redline. Two items to flag up front:

1) The Acme legal team prefers explicit language that Redwood will provide 30 days' notice for any new subprocessor and allow Acme the right to object (we'd request the contract include the ability to require termination of the subprocessor for processing Acme data in cases where Acme's objection is reasonable).

2) On transfers: Acme is sensitive about any patient-related metadata leaving the US without additional safeguards. Where transfers outside the US occur, we need to confirm what legal mechanism applies (SCC + technical controls or other safeguards). If Redwood uses hosted models that call external vendor APIs, please confirm whether those parts of the pipeline ever touch unredacted patient data.

Attached: Acme_DPA_Redline_2025-08-01.docx (redlines)

Can you confirm those two points and let us know approximate timing for a final DPA? Procurement will want the DocuSign link in hand by Aug 11.

Thanks —
Sarah
Senior Counsel, Acme Health
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 4 Aug 2025 11:45:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA + subprocessors list (security details)

Hi Sarah / team —

Thanks for the redline — wanted to address the two items directly:

1) Subprocessor notice / objection: we provide 30 days' advance notice for new subprocessors and maintain a published list. Our standard practice is to include an objection right with a "remediation/termination" path; however, we are not able to promise unilateral termination of a subprocessor without evaluating technical feasibility and contractual constraints (many of our cloud providers are required for service continuity). We can agree to escalate objections and work with you on mitigation including contractual commitments with the subprocessor where feasible.

2) Transfers and hosted models: Redwood's core inference pipelines that process customer content for hosted and dedicated deployments are run on customer-selected regions when requested. For Acme's deployment (US region requested in the SOW), customer content will remain in US regions. We do occasionally use third-party model providers for some optional features — we do not send unredacted patient identifiers to third-party APIs unless explicitly configured by the customer.

Compliance artifacts: we can provide SOC 2 Type II report (stub attached) under NDA and complete a security questionnaire.

Attachments: SOC2_TypeII_2025_stub.pdf

If Acme needs stronger contractual language around subprocessor termination, we can route the request to Legal for consideration; let us know specific redline language and we'll respond.

Best,
Monica Patel
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
